When a consumer asks this company to explain a decision the ADMT made about them, the response has to name the specific purpose the ADMT served for that consumer — not a generic company-wide statement (11 CCR § 7222(b)(1)). The CPPA's Final Statement of Reasons ties this directly to why the risk-assessment rules use the same standard: "identifying a purpose in non-generic terms is necessary to identify relevant risks and benefits in a risk assessment and to ensure consumers understand how an ADMT was used with respect to them." The same specificity that a risk assessment needs to actually evaluate a purpose is what a consumer needs to understand a decision made about them. A response that repeats the company's general mission statement does not meet this standard. Section 5 addresses whether this company's access response describes the ADMT's purpose specifically enough. (California Privacy Protection Agency, Final Statement of Reasons, CCPA Updates, Cyber, Risk, ADMT, and Insurance Regulations, 11 CCR § 7222(b)(1), Appendix p. 67.)
